@graph.name: Co-Packer Packaging Automation for Contract Packagers | TRF
@graph.description: Co-packer automation for contract packagers: flexible case packing and palletizing for high SKU mix and frequent changeovers. Talk with our Sales Engineer.

acceptedAnswer.text: A cobot is a collaborative robot, an arm designed for shared workspaces at moderate speeds. In palletizing, a cobot picks each case from the infeed conveyor and places it on the pallet in a stored pattern. TRFCobot puts one in a standardized cell built for co-packers and contract manufacturers with short runs and frequent SKU changes.

mainEntity.name: Can a Cobot Palletizer Handle Multiple SKUs and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Built for high-mix palletizing, TRFCobot stores multiple recipes, pallet patterns and SKU changes for lines of about 1 to 10 cases per minute with cases up to about 22 lb, so each customer's pattern can be stored and recalled. TRF confirms that the end-of-arm tool and reach cover every case in your mix. Higher rates move to TRFCompact or TRFSpeed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Case Packer Handle Pouches, Trays and Thermoformed Packages in the Same Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within its validated range. TRFRapidpack handles pouches, pillow bags, flow packs, thermoformed packages, trays, cartons, cups, tubs and small packaged products, and changes products and patterns through recipes with reduced mechanical adjustments. That breadth is what makes flexible case packing serve several customers on one line. TRF validates the full product list before quoting.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine. TRFOnepack works this way, with one controls platform, fewer interfaces and a smaller footprint than three separate machines. For a contract packager, that means one machine to learn and maintain when the line changes customers.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a palletizer built for it. TRFSubzero palletizes in frozen areas below 32°F, which fits co-packers that run frozen food or ice cream programs. The Custom Foods case study documents robotic palletizing below freezing. TRF validates the layout and the equipment for each cold application before quoting.

mainEntity.name: How Should a Co-Packer Calculate Payback on Packaging Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with the labor hours the equipment replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost, including electricity and maintenance. Then calculate against utilization across contracts, not one product, count changeover time recovered, and compare the payback with the length of the contracts behind the line. The payback calculator gives a first estimate.
